lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is moving house. My sister and her fiancé just moved in together.
Exciting! Was it a big move?
Huge. She had forty boxes. I helped her pack the whole weekend — on a video call.
[laugh] Very helpful, Sam.
I gave advice! Mostly: "Do you really need this?" She had to declutter.
When I left my parents' flat, I learned that lesson too. I had kept every school notebook.
When was that?
Three years ago. It's not so common here to move out before you marry, so my mum cried for a week.
Really?
Really. But now she loves visiting me. For me it was a fresh start.
When I moved to Baku, I brought only two suitcases. Everything else stayed in my mum's garage.
And your first flat here?
Terrible! The rent was too high, and the furniture was older than me.
And the landlord?
He kept half of my deposit when I left. He said the sofa was damaged. It was damaged when I arrived!
That happens a lot. Take photos on the first day. Always.
Lesson learned. My flat now is small, but it's near the sea, and the neighbours are lovely.
So it was easy to settle in this time.
Very easy. When I come back from a trip and open the door, I think: home sweet home.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: how many times have you moved — and what was the hardest part?
Mine: carrying a washing machine up five floors. See you next time!
Bye for now!
